title: Line-by-line verification ledger for the three supplied product references
method: 1. Parse the identifier out of the supplied URL (path segment).
2. Test the identifier against Amazon's published ASIN format (10 alphanumeric characters) — source S11.
3. Follow the supplied short link to its target and record the resolved product page; also request https://www.amazon.com/dp/<identifier> to test whether the code itself is an ASIN — S13.
4. Test whether the supplied host is a real Amazon-controlled host: DNS resolution + IANA root-zone record for the '.amazon' TLD — source S12.
5. Any attribute not returned by an official page is left null and flagged; nothing is inferred.
6. Re-read each supplied link in a separate session (2026-11-14) and compare the resolved page title and breadcrumb against the recorded values before publishing any product field.

flags.title: Supplied code B04G1MEwY is a short-link token, not an ASIN; product identity resolved to B0CDY277D3
flags.detail: CORRECTED 2026-11-14. An earlier pass recorded this as a blocker on the grounds that amazon.com/dp/B04G1MEwY returns Amazon's 'Page Not Found' document. That conclusion was wrong in its inference, though the observation was right: the code is 9 characters, so it is not an ASIN, but it is a valid link.amazon short-link token, and following it lands on the product page for B0CDY277D3. Identity is therefore verified and no longer blank. What remains is a naming caution: the token must never be presented as an ASIN, and any future link must carry a real Associates tag.
flags.action: Resolved: product identity confirmed from the official page. Kept as an informational record of the correction so the earlier wrong conclusion is not silently overwritten.

flags.detail: Third-party summaries quote a Participation Requirements clause requiring an adjacent date/time stamp when pricing or availability is displayed from Data Feeds / PA API or refreshed less often than hourly. That clause was not in the text retrieved by this session.
flags.action: Read the Participation Requirements section of the Program Policies before shipping any price display; the platform blocks price display until then (see platform.policy PRICE_DISPLAY gate).

flags.detail: Figures such as 1 transaction per second and 8,640 transactions per day for new credentials are third-party claims; the official rates page was not retrieved by this session.

flags.title: Two official Creators API pages describe marketplace access differently
flags.detail: The onboarding page says you may only use the API for the marketplace you registered in; the FAQ says credentials work globally with an x-marketplace header but require a valid Partner Tag and regional API approval. The platform therefore requires an explicit, separately configured tag per marketplace.
flags.action: Confirm the current wording for your locale before enabling a second marketplace.

flags.title: Two design systems were merged: index.html and executive-summary.html referenced 26 CSS classes that styles.css did not define
flags.detail: Detected by a class-coverage check (tools/check_links.py --css): 'brandmark' vs 'brand-mark', plus .crumb, .disclosure, .metric-head, .table-note, .pill/.tag variants and others. The pages were live but unstyled for those blocks.
flags.action: Fixed in this pass by appending an additive compatibility block to styles.css (no prior rule was changed or removed).

flags.title: Two GitHub Pages publishers are configured at once
flags.detail: The repository Pages setting is the legacy branch build (source: main, path /, status built) while .github/workflows/pages.yml also deploys through actions/deploy-pages@v4. The run log shows the legacy 'pages build and deployment' job repeatedly cancelled when the Actions workflow deploys, and earlier workflow runs failed before jobs. Content is currently published either way.
flags.action: Pick exactly one publisher. Recommended: keep the Actions workflow and set Settings → Pages → Build and deployment to 'GitHub Actions'. Left unchanged by this session because it is an account-level setting that other sessions may also be touching.

flags.detail: Amazon's own Associates FAQ page refers to the retirement of Mobile Popover, Banners, and Native Shopping Ads; this session read only that page's section structure, not the answer text, so it is recorded as unconfirmed.
flags.action: Confirm before building any widget/banner-based placement; this site uses text links only.

flags.title: Price, availability and deal fields are withheld by policy, not by lack of data
flags.detail: The product pages display price, availability and protection-plan figures, and they were seen while verifying identity. They are not published here: Participation Requirements 2(b) restricts how Amazon-sourced content may be obtained and displayed, and 6(y) bars tracking, selecting or capturing Amazon prices without a written agreement. Any price comparison or deal-alert feature is therefore out of scope until that agreement exists.
flags.action: No action required for the merge: this item is recorded so the limitation is visible to a reader, and closed only by an official source or an account setting.

flags.title: Star ratings and review counts may only come from the Creators API
flags.detail: Participation Requirements 6(t) permits displaying Amazon reviews or star ratings only when the data is obtained through the API. Ratings were visible on the pages but are withheld. Until API access exists, no rating-based ranking, 'high-converting' label or review-velocity metric can be published.
flags.action: No action required for the merge: this item is recorded so the limitation is visible to a reader, and closed only by an official source or an account setting.

flags.title: Listing title and breadcrumb are reproduced from the product page rather than approved content
flags.detail: The published product name and category path were read from the page itself. Participation Requirements 2(b) allows Product Information obtained through SiteStripe or the API, and content must not be altered; titles here are reproduced verbatim except that a registered-trademark symbol and a degree symbol were normalised in one title, which is the kind of alteration the policy discourages. The same reasoning that withholds prices arguably applies to these fields.
flags.action: Re-source these fields from SiteStripe or the API, or withhold them as prices are withheld.

flags.title: Which commission band Amazon assigns to these ASINs is unconfirmed: Kitchen 4.50% or Home 3.00%
flags.detail: Table 1 lists 'Physical Books, Kitchen, Automotive' at 4.50% and 'Toys & Games, Furniture, Home, Home Improvement...' at 3.00%. The breadcrumb's top node is 'Home & Kitchen', which spans both labels, and the rate Amazon actually applies is decided per item by Amazon, not by the browse path. The published 4.50% is recorded as the Kitchen-band reading with this flag attached; it is not a per-ASIN confirmation and no earning figure is derived from it.
flags.action: Confirm the applied rate for each ASIN in the Associates Central earnings report, then drop or correct the published value.

flags.title: No Associates Partner Tag exists, so nothing published can earn
flags.detail: The resolved product URLs carry no tag parameter and no Associates account is connected to this repository. The link builder refuses to emit a link with a placeholder tag, and the site therefore publishes no monetised outbound link at all. This is the single blocking item for the business goal, ahead of any feature work.
flags.action: Register the Site in Associates Central, record the returned tag in the config, then rebuild; the link layer validates the tag format before it will emit a tagged link.

flags.title: Amazon text notice (IP License 2(k)) is now required wherever listing titles are displayed
flags.detail: Raised by another session as site flag F-24 and adopted here. This site reproduces Amazon listing titles as product labels, which is Product Advertising Content consisting of text, so the 'CERTAIN CONTENT ... COMES FROM AMAZON ... PROVIDED AS IS' notice must appear in plain view. The notice is now rendered on every generated page, driven by data/content.json (site_disclaimer) so it can be withdrawn without a template change if a reviewer concludes titles are not Program Content.
flags.action: Have counsel confirm the notice wording and placement; the engine control TEXT-01 now flags any draft that cites Amazon text without it.

flags.title: Agent Terms apply to the engine's own retrieval path
flags.detail: IP License Section 4 requires a software agent that accesses Program Content to identify itself as an agent and forbids concealing that fact or circumventing access limits. The engine currently performs no live retrieval (research returns 'not run' unless --online is passed and credentials exist), so nothing is in breach today. Before any live fetching is enabled, the client must send an explicit Agent/<name> user-agent token and must respect, not route around, rate limits and robot restrictions.
flags.action: When wiring live retrieval, set an identifying user agent and keep the F-50 sourcing decision open rather than scraping to fill blanks.
